points.description: Gives one valid advantage of separating declaration from definition, e.g. clearer/easier to read and understand code, easier changing/debugging/overriding of functions, better modularity, or separation of abstraction (interface) from implementation.
points.partial_credit: Half if the advantage is vague but clearly on the right track (e.g. 'makes code better organised').

points.description: Gives a second, different valid advantage from the same set (clarity/readability, easy changing/debugging/overriding, modularity, abstraction separated from implementation).
points.partial_credit: Half if vague but on the right track.

rubric.notes: Full marks for two different valid advantages in any wording, such as readability, easier modification/debugging, modularity, or separating interface from implementation. One valid advantage gets 1 mark. Wrong or extra remarks do not cost marks; repeating the same advantage in different words counts only once.
